answer: Each agent can earn voting weight only by completing a unique, costly task whose result is checked against public data and accepted by independent validators. The protocol caps credit per verified identity and slashes a bonded deposit when validators prove an agent reused evidence or colluded. A kernel of honest validators can therefore reject a swarm of fresh accounts; the attacker must fund deposits and real work for every identity, pushing the cost of a Sybil attack toward its zenith. A haven for cheap fabricated identities offers no shortcut past those checks.
